startup.name: Fuse AI
startup.description: AI native outbound sales platform that bundles lead data, enrichment, multichannel sequencing, buying signals and AI execution in one system for revenue teams. Twelve person team in San Francisco, Winter 2025 batch. Buyers are sales and revenue teams paying per seat or per credit, competing with the stacks of Clay, Apollo and AI SDR vendors.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up for a team of twelve, which is unusually large and suggests shipped product, and a B2B AI sales pitch that fits YC's agent theme. Down because AI outbound is one of the most crowded YC wedges, with Topo, Champ, Ciro, Persana and Bluebirds in earlier batches, and an all in one pitch is hard to tell from Apollo or Clay. Net about 3 percent; the company is already in the batch so this is for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that AI outbound and all in one GTM platforms are crowded, that Apollo and Clay already bundle data, enrichment and sequencing, and that the pitch does not name a customer segment that Fuse serves better. Past AI SDR companies from the same wedge produced small rounds or sold early, so partners would ask what is different.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 22.4 months, from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, and counts a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it. Anchor 0.59 for B2B and 0.75 for the tiny Sales tag cohort. A 22 month window covers the 2022 and later p75 time to seed (14 to 20 months), so about 85 percent of eventual seeds fit: 0.59 times 0.85 is 0.50, which is 0.85x of the B2B anchor. A team of twelve and a hot sector are not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, common for AI sales tools that sell self serve.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of 3.5M to 4.1M, the typical result for a live product.
Strong seed for an AI native company with a live product and a team of 12 or more, matching the winners test band shape.
Large seed after fast revenue growth; Clay level attention is rare for a new entrant.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if Fuse cannot show recurring revenue that survives churn, because AI outbound customers cancel quickly when reply rates fall and spam filters tighten. Ciro, Persana AI and Bluebirds reached seed rounds in this exact wedge but then sold or stalled, Champ and Topo show no round beyond the YC deal in their records, and Slik shut down. Investors will want proof that the platform is not a thin layer over Clay and an email tool.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside 22 months of starting would make Fuse a category leader in AI sales within two years, ahead of Clay and Apollo that already hold the customers. None of the AI outbound YC analogs in the data came near it, and the Series C base rate rests on only three B2B companies, so the number is a floor rather than an estimate.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most outcomes in this wedge are an early acquisition by a larger sales tool or a stall after seed, as Ciro, Persana AI and Bluebirds show. A venture sized outcome needs a differentiated data or signal asset that Clay and Apollo cannot copy, and the twelve person team would need to find it before its cash runs out, which is why the failure share is set at half.

killers.risk: Customers churn when AI outbound reply rates fall and email deliverability rules tighten
killers.evidence: Mass AI generated outreach raises spam filtering and lowers reply rates, and AI SDR vendors report high churn after the first months.
killers.mitigation: Focus on signal driven, low volume, high intent outreach and report booked meetings, not emails sent.

killers.risk: Clay, Apollo and ZoomInfo bundle the same data and automation and out distribute a new entrant
killers.evidence: Clay raised a Series B of 46M in June 2024 and Apollo sells a 230M contact database with sequencing in the same product, so an all in one pitch meets entrenched leaders.
killers.mitigation: Choose a vertical or a proprietary signal source that the horizontal tools do not cover.

killers.risk: Team of twelve burns cash before revenue proves the all in one scope
killers.evidence: Building data, enrichment, multichannel sending and execution needs many integrations and a large team, which raises monthly burn.
killers.mitigation: Narrow to one workflow first and sell it, then expand.

technical_complexity.rationale: Enrichment, sequencing and LLM message writing are well known building blocks and a twelve person team can ship them in three months. The hard parts are data quality, deliverability and integrations rather than research, so complexity is not a moat.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents already own the data and the sequencing, and adding agent features is a short build. A new entrant has no distribution edge unless it wins a segment, so the risk of being copied or squeezed is high.

evidence.claim: Clay raised a 46M Series B in June 2024, showing large paid demand for outbound data and workflow tools
Apollo sells a 230M contact database with multichannel sequences at prices starting near 49 dollars per month, evidence of paid demand and price pressure

narrative.headline: A crowded AI outbound pitch with a large team; a seed inside 22 months is likely but a Series A is not.
narrative.general_summary: Fuse AI bundles data, enrichment and AI sequencing for sales teams, a wedge with strong paid demand but heavy competition from Clay, Apollo and many AI SDR startups. For 2022 and later B2B YC companies about 59 percent reach a seed and most do so inside 22 months, so the seed estimate is 50 percent for the window. Direct YC analogs (Ciro, Persana AI, Bluebirds) raised a seed then sold, which pulls the Series A chance well below the anchor. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: The input has no traction data; seed odds assume a normal Winter 2025 B2B company with a live product and 12 people.
Window 22.4 months; seed means a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it.
Sales tag cohort has n=8 and is an anecdote; the B2B cohort is the main anchor.
